h1: Lymphatic Buccal Facial Massage in Huntington Beach
intro: A Lymphatic Buccal Facial Massage combines gentle lymphatic drainage techniques with buccal, or intraoral, massage, where a gloved practitioner works certain facial muscles from inside the mouth as well as from the outside. It is for people who want to relieve facial and jaw tension, reduce temporary puffiness and enjoy a more sculpted, refreshed look without needles or downtime.
whatIs: This treatment brings together two massage styles. Lymphatic drainage techniques use light, rhythmic strokes across the face and neck to encourage the movement of fluid that can make the face look puffy, especially in the morning or after travel, salty meals or poor sleep. Buccal massage then focuses on the muscles of the cheeks and jaw. Wearing gloves, the practitioner places a finger inside the mouth and works the muscle between the inside and outside hands, reaching areas that regular facial massage cannot.

Many people come in because they clench their jaw, carry stress in their face or simply want their features to look more defined for an event. The effects are temporary and tend to build with a series of sessions, so it works well as part of an ongoing self-care routine. It is a relaxation and beauty treatment, not a medical or detox therapy. Every service at CAIR SPA is performed under the oversight of Tran Plastic Surgery, led by Dr. Tuan Tran, a triple board-certified plastic, reconstructive and hand surgeon whose practice is in the same Huntington Beach building.

steps.title: Consultation
steps.text: We review your goals, health history, recent dental work and any injectables or facial treatments, so we can confirm the massage is right for you and plan how much pressure to use.

steps.title: Lymphatic drainage
steps.text: After cleansing, light, rhythmic strokes are applied across the face and neck to help ease puffiness and prepare the muscles for deeper work.

steps.title: Buccal massage
steps.text: Wearing gloves, the practitioner works the cheek and jaw muscles from inside the mouth together with outside techniques, adjusting pressure to your comfort.

steps.title: Finish and aftercare
steps.text: The session ends with soothing outer massage and skincare, plus simple tips such as drinking water and avoiding heavy salt to help you enjoy the refreshed look longer.

expect.before: Come with a clean face if you can. Tell us if you have had neurotoxin or filler injections recently, since many providers suggest waiting about 2 weeks before facial massage. Also let us know about recent dental work, cold sores or any active infection, certain medical conditions, or if you are pregnant, so we can check whether to adjust or reschedule.
expect.during: The outer lymphatic work feels light and relaxing. The buccal portion can feel intense, especially on tight jaw muscles, but you can ask for lighter pressure or a pause at any time. The full session is about 60 minutes.
expect.after: Many people notice their face looks less puffy and more defined right away. Some feel mild tenderness in the jaw or cheeks for a day, similar to after a deep massage. There is typically no downtime, and you can return to your normal routine.

faqs.q: How much does a Lymphatic Buccal Facial Massage cost?
faqs.a: Price depends on your plan, including whether you book a single session or a series. We give you an exact quote at your free consultation.
Most people have no downtime and can go right back to their day. Some feel mild jaw or cheek tenderness for a short time afterward, which typically fades on its own.

faqs.q: How long do the results last?
faqs.a: Results are temporary. The less puffy, more sculpted look is often most noticeable for a few days, and it varies from person to person. Many people choose a series of sessions to build and maintain the effect.

It should not be painful, but it can feel intense, especially if your jaw muscles are tight from clenching or stress. Pressure is adjusted to your comfort, and you can ask to slow down or stop at any time.

faqs.q: Can I get this massage after Botox® or fillers?
faqs.a: Many providers recommend waiting about 2 weeks after neurotoxins such as Botox®, Dysport® or Xeomin®, or after dermal fillers, before deep facial massage. Let us know the date of your last treatment and we will help you time your session.

faqs.q: Who is a good candidate for a Lymphatic Buccal Facial Massage?
faqs.a: Most healthy adults who want to ease facial tension or temporary puffiness are good candidates. If you have an active infection or cold sore, recent dental work, recent injectables or certain medical conditions, we may suggest waiting. If you are pregnant, please check with us and your doctor first.
